newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh SEC chief says has resigned.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh SEC chief says has resigned.

text.p: The chairman of Bangladesh's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Harunur Rashid, said he had resigned in protest against "lack of cooperation and support" by the government in his efforts to revamp the nation's capital markets.

"I decided to resign because I had not been getting cooperation from the relevant authorities. If I am not able to contribute to the development of the capital market, (then) why should I be holding my post," said Rashid.

Rashid said he had submitted the letter of resignation to the government on June 29, after serving as SEC chief for about 11 months, but was still awaiting a reply. Rashid said he had submitted the letter of resignation to the government on June 29, after serving as SEC chief for about 11 months, but was still awaiting a reply. "We have received his resignation letter. We are examining his complaints. The fate of the letter has yet to be decided," one finance ministry official told Reuters on Wednesday. "The final decision will come from the Prime Minister."
